hooks.name: Auto Raise PR on Task Completion
hooks.description: Automatically runs the full PR workflow after a spec task is marked completed. Stages files, runs tests, commits, pushes the branch, and raises a PR with the ready-for-review label — no manual skill invocation needed.

action.prompt:
A spec task just completed. Automatically run the full PR workflow now — no need for the developer to invoke the raise-pr skill manually.

## Auto PR Workflow

Work through every step in order. Do not skip a step if an earlier one fails — fix it first.

### Step 1 — Confirm branch
Run: `git branch --show-current`
- Branch must match `feature/task-<n>-<slug>`.
- If on `main`, stop and tell the developer to switch to the correct feature branch.

### Step 2 — Inspect staged/unstaged changes
Run: `git status --short` and `git diff --name-only HEAD`
- Confirm no `.env` file is staged. If it is, unstage it immediately and add it to `.gitignore` before continuing.
- Confirm all changed files belong to this task's scope.

### Step 3 — Run tests
- If any `tm-backend/` files changed: run `pytest` from `tm-backend/`. All tests must pass.
- If any `tm-frontend/` files changed: run `npx vitest --run` from `tm-frontend/`. All tests must pass.
- If tests fail, fix the failures before continuing — do not raise the PR with a broken test suite.

### Step 4 — Run the pre-PR code review checklist
Check every item:
**Folder structure**: backend files in correct layer (routers/services/models/schemas/db/tests), frontend in correct folder (pages/components/hooks/api/constants/utils), CSS Modules co-located.
**Backend**: Mapped/mapped_column style, no Base.metadata.create_all(), env vars via Settings, 403 before 404, no print(), pinned requirements.
**Frontend**: JWT in React state only, no direct client.js import in components, useTasks owns task state, STATUS_VALUES constant used, no inline style except dynamic, no Tailwind.
**Security**: no secrets staged, no .env committed.

If any ISSUES are found, fix them before proceeding to Step 5.

### Step 5 — Stage files
Stage only the files that changed for this task. Never run `git add .` blindly.
Verify with: `git diff --staged --name-only`

### Step 6 — Commit
Use this exact format:
```
feat(task-<n>): <short imperative description>

Implements <task title> as per .kiro/specs/task-manager-app/tasks.md
Closes #<github-issue-number>
```

### Step 7 — Push the branch
```
git push -u origin feature/task-<n>-<slug>
```

### Step 8 — Raise the PR
Use the GitHub CLI with the `ready-for-review` label. Create the label first if it does not exist:
```
gh label create "ready-for-review" --color "0075ca" --description "Task complete, awaiting at least 1 approved review before merge" --repo krishna-1210/task-manager-app
```
Then raise the PR:
```
gh pr create \
  --title "feat(task-<n>): <short description under 70 chars>" \
  --body "## Summary

Implements Task <n> — <task title>.

<1–2 sentence description of what was built>

## Changes

- \`<file>\` — <what it does>

## Testing

- [ ] \`pytest\` passes (backend)
- [ ] \`vitest --run\` passes (frontend)

## Review Gate

**Minimum 1 approved review is required before this PR can be merged.**

Closes #<github-issue-number>" \
  --base main \
  --head feature/task-<n>-<slug> \
  --label "ready-for-review"
```

### Step 9 — Do NOT close the task
After the PR is raised, the task status must stay open as **ready for review** — do not mark it as closed or done. Inform the developer:
> "PR raised and labelled **ready-for-review**. At least 1 approved review is required before merging. The task will remain open until the PR is merged."

### What to tell the developer after the PR is raised
Output a short summary:
- Branch pushed: `feature/task-<n>-<slug>`
- PR URL (from `gh pr view --json url`)
- Label applied: `ready-for-review`
- Next step: share the PR link for review; merge only after ≥ 1 approval
